mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the hybridisation type, molecular geometry, and ideal bond angle for species that exhibit sp, sp2 and sp3 hybridisation?

options.A: sp hybridisation leads to linear geometry with a 180° bond angle; sp2 gives trigonal planar geometry with a 120° bond angle; sp3 gives tetrahedral geometry with a 109.5° bond angle.
options.B: sp hybridisation leads to tetrahedral geometry with a 109.5° bond angle; sp2 gives linear geometry with a 180° bond angle; sp3 gives trigonal planar geometry with a 120° bond angle.
options.C: sp hybridisation leads to trigonal planar geometry with a 120° bond angle; sp2 gives tetrahedral geometry with a 109.5° bond angle; sp3 gives linear geometry with a 180° bond angle.
options.D: sp hybridisation leads to linear geometry with a 180° bond angle; sp2 gives tetrahedral geometry with a 109.5° bond angle; sp3 gives trigonal planar geometry with a 120° bond angle.

mcqs.answer: sp hybridisation leads to linear geometry with a 180° bond angle; sp2 gives trigonal planar geometry with a 120° bond angle; sp3 gives tetrahedral geometry with a 109.5° bond angle.
mcqs.explanation: In sp hybridisation one s and one p orbital combine to give two sp hybrids, producing a linear arrangement (180°). In sp2 hybridisation one s and two p orbitals form three sp2 hybrids, giving a trigonal planar shape (120°). In sp3 hybridisation one s and three p orbitals form four equivalent hybrids, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry (109.5°). The other options mix these relationships incorrectly.

mcqs.question: In which of the following molecules is the central atom sp hybridised?
mcqs.explanation: BeCl₂ has a linear shape with a bond angle of 180°, indicating that the central Be atom uses sp hybridisation (one s + one p orbital). BF₃ is trigonal planar (sp²), CH₄ is tetrahedral (sp³), and NH₃ is pyramidal (sp³ with a lone pair).

mcqs.question: Which description correctly defines sp hybridisation?

options.A: Mixing one s and one p orbital to form two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals, giving a linear geometry.
options.B: Mixing one s and two p orbitals to form three equivalent sp² hybrid orbitals, giving a trigonal planar geometry.
options.C: Mixing one s and three p orbitals to form four equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals, giving a tetrahedral geometry.
options.D: Mixing one s, one p and one d orbital to form three spd hybrid orbitals, giving a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

mcqs.answer: Mixing one s and one p orbital to form two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals, giving a linear geometry.
mcqs.explanation: sp hybridisation involves the combination of one s and one p orbital, producing two sp hybrids that are oriented 180° apart, resulting in a linear molecular geometry. Options B, C, and D describe sp², sp³, and spd hybridisations respectively.

mcqs.question: A carbon atom that is sp² hybridised can form how many σ (sigma) and π (pi) bonds respectively?
mcqs.explanation: In sp² hybridisation, one s and two p orbitals combine to give three sp² hybrids, each forming a σ bond. The remaining unhybridised p orbital forms one π bond. Hence the carbon makes three σ bonds and one π bond. The other options do not match this bonding scheme.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes sp³ hybridisation from other types of hybridisation?

options.A: It involves the combination of one s and three p orbitals to form four equivalent sp³ hybrids that adopt a tetrahedral geometry.
options.B: It involves the combination of one s and two p orbitals to form three equivalent sp² hybrids that adopt a trigonal planar geometry.
options.C: It involves the combination of one s and one p orbital to form two equivalent sp hybrids that adopt a linear geometry.
options.D: It involves the combination of one s, one p and one d orbital to form three spd hybrids that adopt a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.

mcqs.answer: It involves the combination of one s and three p orbitals to form four equivalent sp³ hybrids that adopt a tetrahedral geometry.
mcqs.explanation: sp³ hybridisation mixes one s and three p orbitals, yielding four identical hybrid orbitals arranged tetrahedrally (109.5° bond angles). Options B and C describe sp² and sp hybridisations, while D describes spd hybridisation, none of which match the definition of sp³.

mcqs.question: Which hybridisation corresponds to a molecule that exhibits a trigonal planar geometry?
mcqs.explanation: Trigonal planar geometry (bond angles of ~120°) arises from sp² hybridisation, where one s and two p orbitals combine to give three hybrid orbitals lying in one plane. sp gives linear geometry, sp³ gives tetrahedral, and dsp² is associated with square planar geometry.

mcqs.question: In ethene (C₂H₄), each carbon atom is hybridised as:
mcqs.explanation: Each carbon in ethene forms three σ bonds (two C–H and one C–C) and one π bond (part of the C=C double bond). This bonding pattern requires sp² hybridisation, providing three sp² hybrids for σ bonds and one unhybridised p orbital for the π bond. sp would give only two σ bonds, sp³ would give four σ bonds, and dsp² is not relevant here.

mcqs.question: A molecule is linear with a bond angle of 180°, the central atom forms exactly two σ bonds and has no lone pairs. What is the hybridisation of the central atom?
mcqs.explanation: A linear arrangement with two σ bonds and no lone pairs indicates that the central atom uses two sp hybrid orbitals (derived from one s and one p orbital) oriented 180° apart. sp² would give a trigonal planar shape, sp³ a tetrahedral shape, and sp d is not applicable for a simple linear molecule.
